import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 226

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/226](https://www.erdosproblems.com/226)
- [BaSc70] Barth, K. F. and Schneider, W. J., *Entire functions mapping
  countable dense subsets of the reals onto each other monotonically*.
  J. London Math. Soc. (2) (1970), 620--626.
- [BaSc71] Barth, K. F. and Schneider, W. J., *Entire functions mapping
  arbitrary countable dense sets and their complements onto each other*.
  J. London Math. Soc. (2) (1971/72), 482--488.
- [Ha74] Hayman, W. K., *Research problems in function theory: new problems*.
  (1974), 155--180.
-/

namespace Erdos226

/-- A real function preserves rationality. -/
def PreservesRationality (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : ℝ, x ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℚ → ℝ) ↔ f x ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℚ → ℝ)

/--
Is there an entire non-linear function $f$ such that, for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$, $x$ is rational if and only if $f(x)$ is?

Barth and Schneider [BaSc70] proved the stronger result for countable dense subsets of
$\mathbb{R}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 30,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos226.lean"]
theorem erdos_226 : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ F : ℂ → ℂ, Differentiable ℂ F ∧ (∀ x : ℝ, (F x).im = 0) ∧
      (∀ g : AffineMap ℝ ℝ ℝ, (fun x : ℝ => (F x).re) ≠ g) ∧
      PreservesRationality (fun x : ℝ => (F x).re) := by
  sorry

end Erdos226

reformulations.difference: The source excludes complex affine functions F(z) = a₀ + a₁z and states rationality preservation directly for F(x). Lean explicitly requires F to be real-valued on the real axis, applies rationality preservation to its real part, and excludes real affine maps only on that restriction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An entire function is continuous. If it maps rational inputs to rational outputs, its imaginary part vanishes on the dense set ℚ and therefore on all of ℝ. Consequently rationality of F(x) is equivalent to rationality of its real part. Every AffineMap ℝ ℝ ℝ is exactly a function x ↦ ax+b. If the real restriction of a real-valued entire function has this form, the complex identity theorem forces F(z)=az+b everywhere. Conversely, the restriction of a complex affine function has affine real part. A full biconditional between the two existential formulations was proved as Review226.full_formulation_iff in /workspace/review/scratch.lean; its axioms contain no sorryAx.

sources_consulted: P. Erdős, Some unsolved problems, Michigan Math. J. 4 (1957), Problem 24, p. 297: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1957-13.pdf

D. Sato and S. Rankin, Entire functions mapping countable dense subsets of the reals onto each other monotonically, Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. 10 (1974), 67–70; introduction and Theorem 1: https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/S0004972700040636

review.notes: Both declarations were checked. PreservesRationality has the intended bidirectional meaning. Lean boundary checks establish that identity preserves rationality but is excluded by nonlinearity, every constant fails rationality preservation, and squaring fails at √2. The positive answer and research-solved category agree with the literature and problem-status database. The cited formal proof exports an equivalent theorem; its full proof was not rebuilt. Direct access to erdosproblems.com and the Wiley full texts was blocked, so the statement was checked against Erdős’s original Problem 24 and the accessible supporting literature. The exact Hayman 1974 chapter was not accessible; the later Hayman–Lingham text corroborates the relevant dense-set results. The reviewed file was not modified.
